name: Multiplicity of Infection (MOI)
expr: MOI = Number of Infectious Virus Particles/Number of Target Cells

name: Antigenic Drift vs Shift (concept)
expr: drift is gradual mutation of viral surface proteins; shift is a sudden major genetic reassortment

name: Host-Parasite Relationship (concept)
expr: an interaction where the parasite benefits at the expense of the host organism

name: Definitive vs Intermediate Host (concept)
expr: the definitive host harbors the adult/sexual stage of a parasite; the intermediate host harbors its larval stage

name: Prevalence of Infection
expr: Prevalence = Number of Infected Hosts/Total Hosts Examined × 100

name: Parasite Life Cycle (concept)
expr: the sequence of developmental stages a parasite undergoes, often across multiple hosts

name: Vector-Borne Disease (concept)
expr: a disease transmitted to humans or animals by an intermediate carrier organism, such as a mosquito

name: Ectoparasite vs Endoparasite (concept)
expr: ectoparasites live on the host's body surface; endoparasites live inside the host's body

name: Drug Half-Life
expr: t½ = time required for the plasma concentration of a drug to reduce by half

name: Bioavailability
expr: F = (Amount of Drug Reaching Systemic Circulation/Dose Administered) × 100

name: Therapeutic Index
expr: TI = Toxic Dose (TD50)/Effective Dose (ED50)

name: Median Effective Dose (ED50) (concept)
expr: the dose that produces a therapeutic effect in 50% of the population tested

name: Median Lethal Dose (LD50) (concept)
expr: the dose of a substance that is lethal to 50% of a test population

name: Drug Clearance
expr: Clearance = Rate of Drug Elimination/Plasma Drug Concentration

name: Volume of Distribution (Vd)
expr: Vd = Total Amount of Drug in Body/Plasma Drug Concentration

name: Agonist vs Antagonist (concept)
expr: an agonist binds a receptor and activates a response; an antagonist binds but blocks the response

name: Menstrual Cycle Length (concept)
expr: typically about 28 days, divided into follicular, ovulation, and luteal phases

name: Gestation Period (concept)
expr: the duration of pregnancy from fertilization to birth, about 38–40 weeks in humans

name: Fertilization (concept)
expr: the fusion of a sperm cell and an egg cell to form a diploid zygote

name: Spermatogenesis vs Oogenesis (concept)
expr: spermatogenesis produces four sperm cells; oogenesis produces one egg and polar bodies from one parent cell

name: Fecundity (concept)
expr: the potential reproductive capacity of an organism, measured by the number of offspring produced

name: Sexual vs Asexual Reproduction (concept)
expr: sexual reproduction combines genetic material from two parents; asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring from one parent

name: Hormonal Control of Ovulation (concept)
expr: a surge in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg from the ovary

name: Placenta Function (concept)
expr: exchanges nutrients, gases, and waste between mother and fetus during pregnancy

name: Innate vs Learned Behavior (concept)
expr: innate behavior is instinctive and genetically programmed; learned behavior develops through experience

name: Fixed Action Pattern (concept)
expr: an instinctive, stereotyped behavior sequence triggered by a specific stimulus and carried out to completion

name: Habituation (concept)
expr: a decrease in response to a repeated, harmless stimulus over time

name: Classical Conditioning (concept)
expr: learning where a neutral stimulus becomes associated with a meaningful stimulus to trigger a response

name: Territoriality (concept)
expr: behavior in which an animal defends a specific area against intrusion by others of its species

name: Altruism in Animals (concept)
expr: behavior that benefits another individual at a cost to the performer, often explained by kin selection

name: Biodiversity Index (concept)
expr: a measure combining species richness and evenness to quantify biodiversity in an area

name: Shannon Diversity Index
expr: H' = −Σ(pᵢ × ln(pᵢ)), pᵢ = proportion of individuals of species i

name: Species Richness (concept)
expr: the total number of different species present in a given community or area

name: Minimum Viable Population (concept)
expr: the smallest population size at which a species can survive and maintain genetic diversity long-term

name: Habitat Fragmentation (concept)
expr: the breaking up of a large habitat into smaller, isolated patches, reducing species survival chances

name: Extinction Rate
expr: Extinction Rate = Number of Species Lost/Time Period

name: Endangered vs Threatened vs Extinct (concept)
expr: endangered = at high risk of extinction; threatened = likely to become endangered; extinct = no living members remain

name: Carrying Capacity (concept)
expr: the maximum population size an environment can sustainably support given its available resources

name: Muscle Force-Velocity Relationship (concept)
expr: as the load on a muscle increases, the velocity of its contraction decreases

name: Lever Systems in the Body (concept)
expr: bones act as levers, joints as fulcrums, and muscle contractions as the applied force

name: Bone Stress
expr: Stress = Force/Cross-sectional Area, used to assess bone strength under load

name: Gait Analysis (concept)
expr: the study of the mechanics and pattern of human or animal locomotion

name: Terminal Velocity (Falling Body) (concept)
expr: the constant speed reached when gravitational force is balanced by air resistance

name: Bioluminescence (concept)
expr: the production and emission of light by a living organism through a chemical reaction

name: Electromyography (EMG) (concept)
expr: a technique that records the electrical activity produced by skeletal muscles

name: Metabolic Energy Cost of Movement (concept)
expr: the amount of energy expended by an organism to perform physical movement or exercise

name: Crop Yield
expr: Yield = Total Production/Total Cultivated Area

name: Harvest Index
expr: HI = Economic Yield (grain)/Total Biological Yield (plant)

name: Fertilizer Use Efficiency
expr: FUE = Increase in Yield/Amount of Fertilizer Applied

name: Water Use Efficiency (Crops)
expr: WUE = Crop Yield/Total Water Used

name: Selective Breeding (concept)
expr: the process of breeding plants or animals for particular desirable genetic traits

name: Crop Rotation (concept)
expr: growing different crops in succession on the same land to maintain soil fertility and reduce pests

name: Michaelis-Menten Equation
expr: V = (Vmax[S])/(Km + [S])

name: Km (Michaelis Constant) (concept)
expr: the substrate concentration at which reaction velocity is half of Vmax

name: Vmax (concept)
expr: the maximum reaction velocity reached when the enzyme is fully saturated with substrate

name: Lineweaver-Burk Plot (concept)
expr: a double reciprocal plot of 1/V vs 1/[S] used to determine Km and Vmax graphically

name: Turnover Number (kcat)
expr: kcat = Vmax/[E], moles of substrate converted per enzyme molecule per unit time

name: Catalytic Efficiency
expr: Catalytic Efficiency = kcat/Km

name: Competitive Inhibition (concept)
expr: an inhibitor binds the active site, raising the apparent Km while Vmax remains unchanged

name: Non-Competitive Inhibition (concept)
expr: an inhibitor binds a site other than the active site, lowering Vmax while Km remains unchanged

name: Q10 Temperature Coefficient
expr: Q10 = (Reaction Rate at T + 10°C)/(Reaction Rate at T)

name: Enzyme Activity Unit
expr: 1 Unit (U) = amount of enzyme converting 1 µmol of substrate per minute

name: Incidence Rate
expr: Incidence = New Cases/(Population at Risk × Time)

name: Prevalence
expr: Prevalence = Total Cases/Total Population

name: Basic Reproduction Number (R0) (concept)
expr: the average number of secondary infections produced by one infected individual in a fully susceptible population

name: Case Fatality Rate (CFR)
expr: CFR = (Deaths from Disease/Total Confirmed Cases) × 100

name: Herd Immunity Threshold
expr: HIT = 1 − 1/R0

name: Attack Rate
expr: Attack Rate = (New Cases/Population at Risk) × 100

name: Mortality Rate
expr: Mortality Rate = (Total Deaths/Total Population) × 1000 (per 1000 population)

name: Morbidity Rate (concept)
expr: the rate at which disease occurs within a specific population

name: Relative Risk (RR)
expr: RR = Incidence in Exposed Group/Incidence in Unexposed Group

name: Odds Ratio (OR)
expr: OR = (a × d)/(b × c), from a 2×2 exposure-outcome contingency table

name: CRISPR-Cas9 (concept)
expr: a gene-editing technology using a guide RNA to direct the Cas9 enzyme to cut DNA at a specific sequence

name: Restriction Enzyme (concept)
expr: a protein that cuts DNA at specific recognition sequences

name: Recombinant DNA (concept)
expr: DNA formed by artificially combining genetic material from two or more different sources

name: Gel Electrophoresis (concept)
expr: separates DNA, RNA, or protein fragments by size as they migrate through a gel under an electric field

name: Transformation Efficiency
expr: TE = Number of Colonies/Amount of DNA Used (µg)

name: Cloning Vector (concept)
expr: a DNA molecule such as a plasmid or virus used to carry foreign genetic material into a host cell

name: Gene Therapy (concept)
expr: introducing, altering, or removing genetic material within a patient's cells to treat or prevent disease

name: Southern Blotting (concept)
expr: a technique used to detect the presence of a specific DNA sequence in a sample

name: PCR Amplification Efficiency
expr: Amplification = (1 + E)ⁿ, E = efficiency, n = number of cycles

name: Tumor Growth (concept)
expr: the increase in tumor size over time, often modeled using exponential or Gompertzian growth curves

name: Tumor Doubling Time
expr: Td = (0.693 × t)/ln(Final Volume/Initial Volume)

name: Cell Cycle Checkpoints (concept)
expr: G1, S, G2, and M checkpoints regulate and monitor progression through the cell cycle

name: Proto-oncogene vs Tumor Suppressor Gene (concept)
expr: mutated proto-oncogenes (oncogenes) promote uncontrolled division; tumor suppressor genes normally restrain division

name: Metastasis (concept)
expr: the spread of cancer cells from a primary tumor to other parts of the body

name: Apoptosis (concept)
expr: programmed cell death that eliminates damaged or unwanted cells in a controlled manner

name: Mitotic Index
expr: MI = (Cells in Mitosis/Total Cells Counted) × 100

name: TNM Staging System (concept)
expr: classifies cancer severity by Tumor size (T), lymph Node involvement (N), and Metastasis (M)

name: Types of Epithelial Tissue (concept)
expr: squamous, cuboidal, and columnar, each occurring as simple (single layer) or stratified (multiple layers)

name: Connective Tissue (concept)
expr: tissue that supports, binds, and protects other tissues and organs, e.g. bone, cartilage, blood

name: Muscle Tissue Types (concept)
expr: skeletal (voluntary, striated), smooth (involuntary, non-striated), cardiac (involuntary, striated)

name: Nervous Tissue (concept)
expr: tissue made of neurons and glial cells that generates and transmits electrical signals

name: Basement Membrane (concept)
expr: a thin extracellular layer that separates epithelial tissue from the underlying connective tissue

name: H&E Staining (concept)
expr: Hematoxylin stains cell nuclei blue/purple; Eosin stains cytoplasm and extracellular matrix pink

name: Tissue Section Thickness (Microtome)
expr: typically 4–10 micrometers (µm) for standard light microscopy

name: Cell Density in Tissue
expr: Cell Density = Number of Cells/Area or Volume of Tissue

name: Fertilization (concept)
expr: the fusion of sperm and egg nuclei to form a diploid zygote

name: Cleavage (concept)
expr: rapid mitotic division of the zygote into smaller cells without an overall increase in size

name: Blastula Stage (concept)
expr: a hollow ball of cells formed after cleavage, enclosing a fluid-filled cavity called the blastocoel

name: Gastrulation (concept)
expr: the process that forms the three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm

name: Germ Layer Derivatives (concept)
expr: ectoderm → skin/nervous system, mesoderm → muscle/bone, endoderm → gut lining and associated organs

name: Neurulation (concept)
expr: the formation of the neural tube from ectoderm, which later develops into the brain and spinal cord

name: Gestation Period (concept)
expr: the time between fertilization and birth, which varies widely between species

name: Apgar Score (concept)
expr: a quick newborn health assessment based on Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, and Respiration

name: LD50 (Lethal Dose 50%) (concept)
expr: the dose of a substance required to kill 50% of a test population

name: LC50 (Lethal Concentration 50%) (concept)
expr: the concentration of a substance in air or water that kills 50% of a test population

name: Therapeutic Index
expr: TI = LD50/ED50 (a higher TI indicates a safer drug)

name: Dose-Response Curve (concept)
expr: shows the relationship between the dose of a substance and the magnitude of its biological effect

name: Bioaccumulation (concept)
expr: the gradual buildup of a substance in an organism faster than it can be metabolized or excreted

name: Biomagnification (concept)
expr: the increasing concentration of a toxin at successively higher levels of a food chain

name: Half-Life of a Toxin
expr: t½ = time required for the concentration of a substance in the body to reduce by half

name: No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) (concept)
expr: the highest tested dose of a substance at which no harmful effects are observed

name: Salinity (concept)
expr: the concentration of dissolved salts in seawater, typically measured in parts per thousand (ppt)

name: Photic Zone (concept)
expr: the upper layer of the ocean that receives enough sunlight to support photosynthesis

name: Thermocline (concept)
expr: a layer of the ocean where temperature changes rapidly with increasing depth

name: Primary Productivity (Ocean)
expr: Productivity = Rate of Carbon Fixation by Phytoplankton per Unit Area per Unit Time

name: Coral Bleaching (concept)
expr: loss of symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) from coral tissue, usually caused by stress such as rising temperature

name: Tidal Zonation (concept)
expr: the distribution of marine organisms into distinct bands based on tolerance to tidal exposure

name: Osmoregulation in Marine Organisms (concept)
expr: the process by which marine organisms maintain internal salt and water balance

name: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) (concept)
expr: the amount of dissolved oxygen required by microorganisms to break down organic matter in water

name: Insect Body Segments (concept)
expr: head, thorax, and abdomen form the three main body regions of an insect

name: Metamorphosis Types (concept)
expr: complete metamorphosis (egg-larva-pupa-adult) vs incomplete metamorphosis (egg-nymph-adult)

name: Insect Population Growth Rate
expr: r = (Births − Deaths)/Population Size

name: Pheromone (concept)
expr: a chemical secreted by an insect that influences the behavior of other individuals of the same species

name: Compound Eye (concept)
expr: an eye composed of many individual visual units (ommatidia), providing a wide field of view

name: Economic Injury Level (EIL) (concept)
expr: the pest population density at which the cost of control equals the economic damage caused

name: Insect Exoskeleton (concept)
expr: a hard outer covering made of chitin that supports and protects the insect's body

name: DNA Fingerprinting (concept)
expr: a technique used to identify individuals based on unique patterns in their DNA

name: Short Tandem Repeats (STR) (concept)
expr: short DNA sequences repeated a variable number of times, used for individual identification

name: Postmortem Interval Estimation (concept)
expr: estimating time since death using indicators such as body temperature, rigor mortis, and livor mortis

name: Rigor Mortis (concept)
expr: stiffening of muscles after death due to loss of ATP, typically beginning 2–6 hours after death

name: Algor Mortis
expr: body temperature decreases by approximately 1.5°F (0.83°C) per hour after death (average estimate)

name: Blood Spatter Analysis (concept)
expr: interpreting the pattern, shape, and size of bloodstains to reconstruct events at a crime scene

name: Forensic Entomology (concept)
expr: using insect evidence, such as maggot development stage, to estimate the time since death

name: Systems Biology (concept)
expr: an approach that studies biological systems through the interactions of their components as an integrated network

name: Gene Regulatory Network (concept)
expr: a collection of genes and regulators that interact to control gene expression levels

name: Biological Feedback Loop (concept)
expr: a mechanism where a system's output influences its own input, either amplifying (positive) or stabilizing (negative)

name: Synthetic Biology (concept)
expr: designing and constructing new biological parts, devices, and systems not found in nature

name: Metabolic Flux (concept)
expr: the rate of turnover of molecules through a metabolic pathway

name: Biological Oscillator (concept)
expr: a genetic circuit that produces periodic, rhythmic changes in gene expression over time

name: Systems Robustness (concept)
expr: the ability of a biological system to maintain its function despite internal or external perturbations

name: Synthetic Gene Circuit (concept)
expr: an engineered network of genes designed to perform a specific logical function within a cell

name: Carbon Cycle (concept)
expr: the continuous movement of carbon between the atmosphere, oceans, soil, and living organisms

name: Nitrogen Cycle (concept)
expr: the conversion of nitrogen between atmospheric, soil, and organic forms via fixation, nitrification, and denitrification

name: Nitrogen Fixation (concept)
expr: the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) into ammonia by bacteria or industrial processes

name: Phosphorus Cycle (concept)
expr: the movement of phosphorus through rocks, soil, water, and living organisms, largely without an atmospheric phase

name: Water (Hydrologic) Cycle (concept)
expr: the continuous movement of water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff

name: Carbon Footprint (concept)
expr: the total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly or indirectly by an individual, organization, or product

name: Ecological Footprint (concept)
expr: the area of land and water required to sustainably support an individual's or population's resource use and waste

name: Biomagnification Factor
expr: BMF = Concentration in Organism/Concentration in Diet

name: Trophic (Ecological) Efficiency
expr: approximately 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next (the "10% rule")

name: Net Primary Productivity (NPP)
expr: NPP = Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) − Respiration (R)
